content.value_statement: Single-cell researchers need reliable patterns for querying large Census datasets. This skill provides focused guidance for metadata filters, expression retrieval, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides opening versioned CELLxGENE Census data with context managers.
Shows metadata exploration for datasets, tissues, diseases, and cell types.
Explains obs and var filters for cell and gene queries.
Demonstrates AnnData retrieval and out-of-core query patterns.
Covers PyTorch dataloaders and Scanpy workflow integration.
limitations: Does not include executable helper scripts or automated data retrieval.
Requires a working Python environment with CELLxGENE Census dependencies installed.
Examples may need updates for current Census releases and dataset availability.
Large queries still require user planning for memory and storage limits.

use_cases.title: Explore Tissue Cell Types
use_cases.description: Find available cell types, tissues, diseases, and datasets before loading expression matrices.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analysis Workflows
use_cases.description: Build focused Census queries that return AnnData objects for downstream Scanpy analysis.

use_cases.title: Train Models on Census Data
use_cases.description: Use PyTorch dataloaders and batch processing patterns for machine learning workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Available Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me explore CELLxGENE Census metadata for human lung cells. Show which filters and columns I should inspect first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Focused Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CELLxGENE Census query plan for T cells in COVID-19 samples with marker genes CD4, CD8A, and FOXP3.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an out-of-core CELLxGENE Census workflow for brain cells across multiple genes without loading all data into memory.

prompt_templates.title: Design an ML Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PyTorch training workflow using CELLxGENE Census data to classify cell types with reproducible train and test splits.

output_examples.input: Find B cells from lung tissue and avoid duplicate cells.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend filtering lung metadata for B cells, adding primary-data constraints, and selecting only needed observation columns.

output_examples.input: Analyze marker genes for T cells in disease samples.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide gene metadata lookup, focused expression retrieval, and a compact AnnData-based analysis path.

output_examples.input: Process a query that is too large for memory.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest estimating cell counts first, narrowing filters, or using chunked TileDB-SOMA processing.

best_practices: Filter for primary data unless duplicate-cell analysis is intentional.
Specify a Census version when reproducibility matters.
Explore metadata before loading expression matrices.
anti_patterns: Loading broad expression matrices before checking query size.
Omitting primary-data filters in cross-dataset analyses.
Relying on gene symbols without checking available gene metadata.

faq.question: What data source does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers CZ CELLxGENE Census access patterns for standardized single-cell genomics data.

faq.question: Can it write analysis code?
faq.answer: It provides code-oriented guidance and examples, but users must run and validate code locally.

faq.question: Does it handle very large datasets?
faq.answer: It explains chunked and out-of-core patterns for queries that are too large for memory.

faq.question: Does it support Scanpy workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for loading AnnData objects and using common Scanpy analysis steps.

faq.question: Does it support machine learning workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers experimental PyTorch dataloaders and train-test split patterns.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Using Census data normally requires access to the CELLxGENE Census service from the user environment.
